final_candidates.decision_summary: N388 is a surface residue in the head region commonly implicated in m102.4-class epitopes; introducing a negative charge should disrupt the antibody electrostatic interface while the side chain size change is modest, limiting risk to ephrin-B2/B3 binding.

K389 is adjacent to N388 within the same putative epitope patch; removing a surface lysine's positive charge is a classic escape mechanism and the K-to-Q substitution is sterically conservative, favoring retention of receptor engagement.

Q490 is a surface-exposed head-domain residue; a Q-to-E charge reversal at the epitope periphery can weaken m102.4-class CDR contacts with minimal predicted structural perturbation, though epitope overlap is less certain than for 388/389.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence tools are available, so additional rounds of self-reflection are unlikely to change or improve the heuristic Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed loop residue near the m102.4 conformational epitope; charge/polarity swap can disrupt antibody H-bonding while leaving the central ephrin-B2/B3 pocket intact.
N388 lies in the receptor-binding head region commonly implicated in m102.4-class epitopes; a charge-changing substitution is likely to disrupt antibody binding with modest structural cost.

K389 is adjacent to N388; loss of a surface lysine side-chain charge is a classic escape mechanism while being relatively conservative for receptor binding.
Polar-to-acidic change on a solvent-facing ridge that may reduce m102.4 affinity; positioned away from conserved ephrin contact core.
Q490 is surface-exposed in the head domain; introducing a negative charge can disrupt the electrostatic interface with m102.4-class CDRs.
Conservative aromatic edit that removes a hydroxyl-mediated antibody contact with minimal structural perturbation to receptor interface.
Removing the tyrosine hydroxyl at a surface position can abolish a key hydrogen bond to the antibody paratope while being sterically conservative, supporting receptor binding preservation.
Small side-chain deletion could weaken a polar antibody interaction; risk of proximity to receptor pocket keeps confidence moderate-low.
Near the putative epitope rim; a small conservative change with moderate escape potential.
Loop threonine implicated in conformational neutralizing epitopes; Ala reduces H-bond donor capacity for antibodies with low structural cost.
Conservative surface change that may remove an H-bond/ glycan-adjacent contact within the epitope footprint; low structural risk.
Charge neutralization on surface loop may escape m102.4-class recognition; monitor for effects on folding/salt bridges.
Removing a negatively charged surface residue may create a potential N-glycosylation motif depending on local context; risk of unintended glycosylation and folding effects makes it less attractive.
